question_text: An election is best defined as
option_a: The process by which people choose their representatives
option_b: The process by which a government is overthrown
option_c: The process by which a constitution is amended
option_d: The process by which laws are made
explanation: Election is the process of choosing representatives.

question_text: Suffrage means
option_a: The right to vote
option_b: The right to be voted for
option_c: The right to hold public office
explanation: Suffrage is the right to vote.

question_text: Universal adult suffrage means
option_a: The right of all adult citizens to vote
option_b: The right of only property owners to vote
option_c: The right of only men to vote
option_d: The right of only educated people to vote
explanation: Universal adult suffrage is for all adults.

question_text: A general election is an election in which
option_a: All seats in the legislature are contested
option_d: Only local government officials are elected

question_text: A by-election is an election held to
option_a: Fill a vacancy that has occurred between general elections
option_b: Elect all members of the legislature

question_text: A referendum is a
option_a: Direct vote by the electorate on a specific issue
option_d: Vote to amend a constitution only

question_text: A plebiscite is a
option_a: Direct vote by the electorate on a specific issue
option_d: Vote to amend a constitution only

question_text: A primary election is an election in which
option_a: Party members select their candidates for the general election

question_text: A run-off election is held when
option_a: No candidate wins a majority in the first election

question_text: A recall election is an election in which
option_a: Voters remove an elected official from office

question_text: An electoral system is
option_a: The method by which votes are translated into seats
option_b: The method by which candidates are selected
option_c: The method by which elections are conducted
option_d: The method by which campaigns are financed
explanation: Electoral systems translate votes to seats.

question_text: Which of the following is a type of electoral system?
option_a: First-past-the-post

question_text: The first-past-the-post system is also known as
option_a: Simple majority system

question_text: In the first-past-the-post system, the candidate with
option_a: The highest number of votes wins

question_text: Which of the following is a merit of the first-past-the-post system?
option_a: It is simple and easy to understand

question_text: Which of the following is a demerit of the first-past-the-post system?
option_a: It may not reflect the popular vote

question_text: Proportional representation is a system in which
option_a: Seats are allocated in proportion to votes received
option_b: The candidate with the highest votes wins
option_c: The candidate with the lowest votes wins
explanation: PR allocates seats by vote share.

question_text: Which of the following is a merit of proportional representation?
option_a: It reflects the popular vote

question_text: Which of the following is a demerit of proportional representation?
option_a: It can lead to unstable governments
